getPestDescription.fire-ants: Fire ants are aggressive stinging ants common in southern states. Their painful stings can cause allergic reactions in some people.
getPestDescription.termites: Termites cause billions in property damage annually. They feed on wood and can compromise structural integrity if left untreated.
getPestDescription.mosquitoes: Mosquitoes thrive in humid climates and standing water. They're not just annoying—they can transmit diseases like West Nile virus.
getPestDescription.cockroaches: Cockroaches are resilient pests that contaminate food and trigger allergies. They thrive in warm, moist environments.
getPestDescription.spiders: While most spiders are harmless, some species like black widows and brown recluses pose health risks.
getPestDescription.scorpions: Scorpions are arachnids found in desert regions. Their venomous sting requires medical attention in severe cases.
getPestDescription.ants: Common household ants invade homes seeking food and water. Different species require different treatment approaches.
getPestDescription.rodents: Mice and rats carry diseases and cause property damage by gnawing on wires and structures.
getPestDescription.bed-bugs: Bed bugs are hitchhiking pests that feed on human blood. They're notoriously difficult to eliminate without professional help.
getPestDescription.wasps: Wasps build nests around homes and can sting repeatedly. Their nests pose dangers especially to those with allergies.
getPestDescription.ticks: Ticks attach to humans and pets, potentially transmitting Lyme disease and other illnesses.
getPestDescription.fleas: Fleas infest pets and homes, causing itchy bites and potential disease transmission.
getPestDescription.mice: Mice enter homes through tiny openings, contaminating food and spreading diseases through droppings.
getPestDescription.carpenter-ants: Carpenter ants tunnel through wood to create nests, potentially causing structural damage over time.
